title: Copy
hired_for: An owner hires the copy expert so every ad, page, email and listing says one true thing the buyer cares about, in the buyer's own words, so more people buy and fewer ads get rejected or products sent back.

jobs.job: Write ad copy that brings buyers, not just clicks
jobs.why: The owner pays for every click. Copy that wins attention but not orders raises the cost of each sale and hides it behind a high click rate.

watch.metric: cost per purchase by copy variant, 7 day click, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the 3 newest copy sets cost $41 per purchase against a $32 target. After: sets picked on cost per purchase, not clicks, bring the new ones to $30 within 14 days.
jobs.who_today: media buyer, freelance copywriter or founder

jobs.job: Make the page say what the ad promised
jobs.why: When an ad promises one thing and the page says another, the shopper leaves in seconds and the click is wasted. This drifts every time a page or offer changes.

watch.metric: bounce rate of paid sessions on the landing page, trailing 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 live ads promise free returns and the page no longer says it; paid bounce is 71%. After: headlines match and paid bounce drops to 60% within a week.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or the media buyer when they notice

jobs.job: Check every claim, review quote and guarantee before it ships
jobs.why: One unproven claim can get ads rejected, freeze the account or promise something the business cannot honour. The owner carries that risk, not the writer.

watch.metric: ads rejected for policy, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Meta account quality and Google Ads policy manager

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 ads rejected last month for health claims, 3 days of lost delivery. After: 0 rejections from copy for 60 days.
jobs.who_today: founder, or nobody until a rejection lands

jobs.job: Say the offer and the price in one clear, honest line
jobs.why: A confusing offer or a price framed the wrong way costs sales and can train buyers to wait for discounts. The line must match what the store will actually honour.

watch.metric: add to cart rate on pages carrying the offer, trailing 14 days

drives.metric: gross margin per order after discount

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 different framings of the same 20% offer run at once; add to cart is 6.1%. After: one approved line everywhere, add to cart 7.0% with no deeper discount.

jobs.job: Answer the objection that costs the most sales, worst one first
jobs.why: Shoppers leave over one or two doubts: fit, price, does it work, returns. If the copy answers small doubts and skips the big one, sales stay flat.

watch.metric: product page conversion rate, trailing 14 days
watch.source: Shopify or GA4; proxy: pre-sale tickets by topic in Gorgias

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: sizing is the top pre-sale question and no ad or page answers it; product page conversion 2.4%. After: a sizing line on the page and in 2 ads, conversion 2.8% within 3 weeks.

jobs.job: Rewrite a failing ad in the right order: headline, then price, then offer
jobs.why: Most owners kill a weak ad or cut the price first. Changing the headline first often saves the ad without giving away margin.

watch.metric: cost per purchase on the rewritten ad versus the week before, 7 day click

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a once strong ad is at $48 per purchase. After: a new headline on the same image brings it back to $35 in 7 days, no discount added.

jobs.job: Write email and SMS lines that get clicked and bought
jobs.why: Subject lines, preview text and first lines decide whether a send makes money. Weak lines waste the list the owner paid to build.

watch.metric: click rate and placed order rate per send, first 3 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: campaigns average 1.1% click rate. After: hand-written previews and one clear action per email lift it to 1.6% within 4 sends.

jobs.job: Tell buyers about payment, delivery and returns where they hesitate
jobs.why: Many buyers drop at checkout over cost, delivery time or return risk. A short, true line at that moment keeps them going.

watch.metric: checkout completion rate, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no delivery date or return line near the buy button; checkout completion 48%. After: real delivery dates and free returns shown, 52% within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Keep writing short, plain and in the brand's own voice
jobs.why: Long, fancy copy loses phone readers and makes the brand sound like everyone else. Checking every draft by hand does not scale.

watch.metric: reading grade of copy shipped, trailing 30 days (proxy, scored in code)

drives.metric: click rate and cost per purchase on new ads

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: new copy reads at grade 11 with 9 banned-word catches a week. After: grade 7, near zero catches.

jobs.job: Write the guarantee the business can honour and show it at the buy moment
jobs.why: A strong, true guarantee lowers risk for the buyer. A vague or oversold one either does nothing or costs money in claims.

watch.metric: add to cart to purchase rate, trailing 14 days
watch.source: Shopify or GA4; claims in Gorgias

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the guarantee sits in the footer only. After: one plain line next to the price, add to cart to purchase up from 38% to 41%, claims flat.

jobs.job: Pull or fix any live line whose price, stock or deadline is no longer true
jobs.why: A sale ends or a product sells out but the ad and email still say it. Buyers feel tricked and support tickets pile up.

watch.metric: live ads and pages with a price, stock or deadline that no longer matches the store (checked daily)

drives.metric: pre-sale complaints about price or stock

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 live ads still say 30% off 4 days after the sale ended. After: 0 stale lines, caught within 24 hours.

jobs.job: Write product page copy that turns browsers into buyers
jobs.why: The product page closes the sale. A clear title, benefit bullets and a spec block answer the shopper's questions before they leave.

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: hero product page lists features only, add to cart 7%. After: feature to benefit bullets, add to cart 8.2% in 3 weeks.

jobs.job: Replace vague boasts with real proof
jobs.why: Words like best and premium are ignored. A real star rating, review count, number or test result is believed.

watch.metric: click rate and cost per purchase on ads with a specific proof line versus without, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 70% of live ads use superlatives. After: each carries one checkable fact; cost per purchase 8% lower on the proof versions.

jobs.job: Write Google search ads that lead with product, price or offer
jobs.why: Search ads compete line by line next to rivals. Generic headlines lose the click to the rival with a clearer offer.

watch.metric: search ad click rate and conversion rate, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: search ads repeat the brand name in 5 of 9 headlines, click rate 3.2%. After: product, price and one objection answered, click rate 4.1%.

jobs.job: Get a first set of ad copy from a live product page the same day
jobs.why: New products and restocks wait days for a brief. Each day without ads is a day of lost sales at launch.

watch.metric: days from product going live to first ad live
watch.source: Shopify product created date and Meta ad created date

drives.metric: sales in the first 30 days after launch

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 days from launch to first ad. After: 1 day, with a founder check before it runs.

jobs.job: Write 10 or more real headline options and pick the few worth testing
jobs.why: Testing 2 lines that say the same thing teaches nothing. The owner needs several truly different lines so a test can find a winner.

watch.metric: share of new ads beating the account's median cost per purchase, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 8 new ads beats the median. After: 1 in 5, because each test pits different angles, not synonyms.

jobs.job: Say who the product is not for, to cut returns
jobs.why: Buyers who were never a fit return the product and cost shipping twice. A short honest line keeps them out and builds trust with the rest.

watch.metric: return rate for reasons 'not as expected' or 'did not fit', orders from the last 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9% of orders come back as 'not as expected'. After: 7% within 2 months, conversion flat.

jobs.job: Tell cross-border buyers the real delivery time, duties and currency
jobs.why: Overseas shoppers leave when they cannot see what they will pay or when it arrives. Surprise duties also cause refused parcels.

watch.metric: conversion rate of sessions from outside the home country, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Canada sessions convert at 0.9% versus 2.5% at home. After: delivery days and duty line added, 1.4% in a month.

jobs.job: Build a word bank from real reviews and support tickets
jobs.why: Copy written in the maker's words misses the buyer. The buyer's own phrases, taken from reviews and tickets, stop the scroll and feel true.

watch.metric: 3 second view rate of ads built from customer phrases versus others, trailing 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager; reviews and Gorgias for the phrases

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no shared list of customer phrases. After: 40 phrases on file; ads using them hold a 3 second view rate of 32% versus 26%.

jobs.job: Write bundle and kit copy that sells the set, not the discount
jobs.why: Bundles raise order size only when the buyer sees why the items belong together. A plain percent off just gives away margin.

watch.metric: bundle share of orders and average order value, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the 3 pack sells on 6% of orders. After: one line on what is inside, the real saving and why, 9% of orders.

jobs.job: Ship copy batches ready to upload, with no errors
jobs.why: Batches that fail on upload or break a character limit delay launches and waste the media buyer's day.

watch.metric: rows rejected or truncated per upload batch

drives.metric: days from brief to ads live

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12 of 60 rows fail on the last upload. After: 0 to 2 per batch, ads live the same day.

jobs.job: Keep a winning message alive in new forms when it starts to tire
jobs.why: Owners often drop a winning appeal when an ad tires. Swapping the words and visuals but keeping the appeal usually keeps the sales coming.

watch.metric: cost per purchase of the top 3 appeals, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the best appeal was paused after one ad tired. After: 4 new versions of it run, cost per purchase back to target in 10 days.

jobs.job: Keep a record of what copy shipped and how it did
jobs.why: Without a record, every brief starts from zero and the team repeats losing ideas. A log of claims, angles and results makes the next brief better.

watch.metric: share of new briefs that start from a logged winner, trailing 90 days (proxy)
watch.source: brand brain copy log joined to Meta results

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no log; winners live in one person's head. After: 80% of briefs cite a past winner and its numbers.

jobs.job: Keep marketplace listing copy under the same claim rules as ads
jobs.why: A listing that makes a claim the ads are not allowed to make can get suppressed and confuses buyers. Titles that lead with the search term also rank and convert better.

watch.metric: share of listing visits that buy (unit session percentage) on the top listings, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 listings claim 'clinically proven' with no study on file. After: claims match the approved list, share of visits that buy up from 11% to 12.5%.

jobs.job: Name a new product so the name does some of the selling
jobs.why: A name that says the benefit or story saves ad words and helps people remember and search for it.

watch.metric: click rate on ads that name the product, first 30 days after launch (proxy)
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager; branded searches in Search Console

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a new sock line is named by a SKU code. After: a benefit name, and 300 branded searches in the first month.
